newsitem.title: USA: ENCON to end Pepsi contract, sell assets.
newsitem.headline: ENCON to end Pepsi contract, sell assets.

text.p: ENCON Systems Inc said Thursday it has withdrawn from an agreement with a division of PepsiCo Inc as it prepares to sell all of its assets.
The company said it would stop providing site survey, design and installation services for a national exterior lighting retro-fit program for PepsiCo Food Services.

It said it had received notice from Fleet Bank NA that the bank planned to sell the company's assets in order to cover "certain existing and uncured defaults under the company's loan agreement with Fleet".
The company did not say how much money it owed.
"At this point, we believe that ENCON's interests will best be served by winding down the company in an orderly manner so as to realize as much value as possible," it said.
"Unfortunately, it appears that no value will remain for the company's shareholders following the wind-down," it added.
In May 1996, the company reported a net loss of $0.11 a share for its first quarter against a profit of $0.05.
ENCON Systems, formally based in Hopkinton, Mass, developed and implemented energy efficient systems for commercial, industrial, institutional and residential customers.
